name: Cradle Mountain
name_evidence: Wikivoyage page 'Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park' (a guidebook chapter) and the Discover Tasmania North West page; CROSS-REGION names it 'Cradle Mountain'. Flagship Tasmanian park (World Heritage), so rank 1-2 exemption applies besides its nine spots.
notes: Flagship national park; its walks, lakes and peaks are its spots. Span 65 km so Lake St Clair (about 38 km away) falls inside 75% of it.

spots.name: Dove Lake
spots.bio: The glacial lake beneath Cradle Mountain, reached from the Dove Lake car park, with a shoreline circuit.

spots.name: Cradle Mountain
spots.bio: The 1,545 m dolerite peak that is the park's icon, seen from Dove Lake and climbed as a long day walk.

spots.name: Overland Track
spots.bio: Australia's most famous bushwalk: a 65 km multi-day track from Cradle Mountain south to Lake St Clair.

spots.name: Lake St Clair
spots.bio: Australia's deepest freshwater lake, at the southern end of the Overland Track, with a visitor centre and boat trips.

spots.name: Marion's Lookout
spots.bio: A steep two-hour return climb past Crater Falls and Crater Lake to a lookout over Dove Lake, with chain-assisted sections.

spots.name: Cradle Mountain Summit Walk
spots.bio: The six-hour return scramble from the Dove Lake car park to the summit of Cradle Mountain.

spots.name: Mount Ossa
spots.bio: Tasmania's highest peak at 1,617 m, climbed on a worn side track from Pelion Gap on the Overland Track.

spots.name: Pencil Pine Falls
spots.bio: A short rainforest boardwalk past a waterfall, starting behind the Cradle Mountain Visitor Centre.

spots.name: Waldheim Chalet
spots.bio: Gustav Weindorfer's 1912 chalet, a heritage site in the park reached on a short walk from the road.

spots.name: Echo Point
spots.bio: A lake-shore lookout on a 3-7 hour circuit from Cynthia Bay, with views over Lake St Clair.

name: Devonport
name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Devonport' page (with its own See list) and the 'Western Tasmania' region page; Discover Tasmania North West page. Regional city and Spirit of Tasmania ferry port.
notes: Regional hub and ferry port with eleven kept spots within 75% of a 55 km span.

spots.name: Mersey Bluff
spots.bio: A coastal headland at Devonport with the Mersey Bluff lighthouse, a beach and an evening penguin-viewing area.

spots.name: Bass Strait Maritime Centre
spots.bio: A maritime museum in Devonport covering Bass Strait exploration, shipwrecks and settlement.

spots.name: Don River Railway
spots.bio: A vintage steam railway and pioneer village museum at Don, a short drive from Devonport.

spots.name: Tiagarra Aboriginal Culture Centre
spots.bio: An Aboriginal culture centre at Devonport with a nature trail to rock carvings.

spots.name: Tasmanian Arboretum
spots.bio: A 66-hectare arboretum of temperate trees near Devonport, with water birds and platypus.

spots.name: Lillico Beach
spots.bio: A beach between Devonport and Ulverstone where little penguins walk up the sand each evening.

spots.name: Australian Axeman's Hall of Fame
spots.bio: A museum of woodchopping sport in Latrobe, housed in a building made of local timbers.

spots.name: Sheffield
spots.bio: The Town of Murals, at the foot of Mount Roland, with a permanent collection of large street murals.

spots.name: Mount Roland
spots.bio: A 1,234 m peak above Sheffield with 360-degree views from the top of a strenuous full-day summit walk.

spots.name: Gunns Plains Caves
spots.bio: A limestone cave near Ulverstone with daily guided tours through the day.

spots.name: Leven Canyon
spots.bio: A canyon above the Leven River, with a lookout 275 m above the river reached on a short walk from the car park.

name: Wynyard
name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Wynyard' page (Table Cape, Fossil Bluff, the Rocky Cape coast) and 'Western Tasmania' page; Table Cape tulips are the area's headline.
notes: Six kept places cluster round Wynyard (Table Cape, Fossil Bluff, Rocky Cape NP, North Cave, Sisters and Boat Harbour beaches); without it they would be orphans between Burnie and Stanley.

spots.name: Table Cape
spots.bio: A headland with a lighthouse and lookout above Wynyard, and a tulip farm that blooms in spring.

spots.name: Rocky Cape National Park
spots.bio: A coastal park with Aboriginal shelter caves, a lighthouse and coastal walks between Wynyard and Stanley.

spots.name: Boat Harbour Beach
spots.bio: A small bay beach with turquoise water, about 20 minutes' drive from Wynyard.

spots.name: Sisters Beach
spots.bio: A beach about 30 minutes from Wynyard, the start of the Postmans Track walk to Rocky Cape.

spots.name: Fossil Bluff
spots.bio: A beach in Wynyard with layered sedimentary rock and fossils, and a short uphill walk to a lookout.

spots.name: North Cave
spots.bio: A short walk to an Aboriginal shelter cave in Rocky Cape National Park, near the lighthouse.

name: Burnie
name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Burnie' page lists the penguin centre, garden and Guide Falls; regional city.
notes: Four kept spots in a 15 km radius; Wikivoyage chapter and regional hub. Not a kept candidate itself (no town spot).

spots.name: Little Penguin Observation Centre
spots.bio: A foreshore viewing point at Parsonage Point where guides show little penguins at sunset, October to March.

spots.name: Big Penguin
spots.bio: A giant penguin sculpture on Penguin's Main Street, built for the town's centenary.

spots.name: Emu Valley Rhododendron Garden
spots.bio: A 13-hectare rhododendron garden at Romaine, south of Burnie, open daily.

spots.name: Guide Falls
spots.bio: A waterfall in a picnic reserve 20 minutes south of Burnie, best in winter and spring.

name: Mole Creek Karst National Park
name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Mole Creek' page (the caves and Devils Gullet) and Parks Tasmania; the park is named for the caves. Deloraine and Big Coffee Pot are its gateway spots (Wikivoyage Deloraine page).
notes: Five kept spots; park is the name visitors use for the cave area.

spots.name: Marakoopa Cave
spots.bio: A limestone cave near Mole Creek with a glow-worm display, one of the Karst park's show caves.

spots.name: King Solomon's Cave
spots.bio: A limestone show cave in the Mole Creek Karst area, reached by Liena Road.

spots.name: Devils Gullet
spots.bio: A platform overhanging a sheer cliff near Mole Creek, looking across the Fisher River valley to Cradle Mountain.

spots.name: Deloraine
spots.bio: A historic town on the Meander River and the gateway to Mole Creek, Cradle Mountain and the Highland Lakes.

spots.name: Big Coffee Pot
spots.bio: A giant coffee pot sculpture, an old silo, on the Mole Creek Road at Deloraine.

name: King Island
name_evidence: Discover Tasmania 'Guide to King Island' (tourism brand page)
notes: Seven kept spots (Cape Wickham Lighthouse, Currie, Cataraqui, Calcified Forest, Seal Rocks, Martha Lavinia Beach, King Island Historical Museum); a Bass Strait island visitors fly to and base on. Farthest spot Cape Wickham is ~31 km from the centre, within 75% of a 70 km span. Proposal only: needs description, reasons, tips, months, header (Pipeline C).

spots.name: Cape Wickham Lighthouse
spots.bio: Australia's tallest lighthouse, 48 m, built in 1861 after the Cataraqui wreck, with climbing tours.

spots.name: Currie
spots.bio: King Island's main harbour town, with the visitor centre, the harbour and the old lighthouse keeper's precinct.

spots.name: Cataraqui
spots.bio: Memorial and wreck site of the 1845 barque Cataraqui, Australia's worst peacetime maritime disaster.

spots.name: Calcified Forest
spots.bio: A 30-minute, 1.3 km Great Short Walk through limestone formations left by a calcified forest about 7000 years old.

spots.name: Seal Rocks
spots.bio: Lookout on the island's highest cliffs, about 60 m above the sea, reached by a short walk.

spots.name: Martha Lavinia Beach
spots.bio: North-east coast surf beach, rated among the world's best breaks by Surfing Life, good for beachcombing.

spots.name: King Island Historical Museum
spots.bio: Museum in the old lighthouse keeper's cottage with shipwreck and sealing history and the original Cape Wickham lens.

name: Flinders Island
name_evidence: Discover Tasmania Flinders Island guide (tourism brand page)
notes: Seven kept spots (Strzelecki Peaks, Trousers Point, Wybalenna Chapel, Killiecrankie to The Dock Coast Walk, Killiecrankie Bay, Castle Rock, Furneaux Museum); Strzelecki National Park is a container and not counted. Spots lie within ~35 km of Whitemark. Proposal only.

spots.name: Strzelecki Peaks
spots.bio: Steep 4-5 hour return walk to the 756 m summit of Mount Strzelecki, the island's highest point.

spots.name: Trousers Point
spots.bio: Turquoise beach with a Great Short Walk loop, snorkelling and a walk-in campground at its southern end.

spots.name: Wybalenna Chapel
spots.bio: Chapel and cemetery at Wybalenna, the 1830s-40s settlement where Aboriginal Tasmanians were exiled.

spots.name: Killiecrankie to The Dock Coast Walk
spots.bio: Rocky coastal walk from Killiecrankie to The Dock, past a sea arch at Stackys Bight and Old Man's Head.

spots.name: Killiecrankie Bay
spots.bio: Bay where visitors search the sand at low tide for semi-precious topaz, known as Killiecrankie diamonds.

spots.name: Castle Rock
spots.bio: Beach-hop walk to towering Castle Rock, one of Tasmania's 60 Great Short Walks.

spots.name: Furneaux Museum
spots.bio: Island history museum at Emita, with a muttonbirding shed replica, police cells and a Sydney Cove anchor.
